name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of Merari, who played a role in the post-exilic community of Israel. He is noted as one of the Levites sent to assist Ezra in the book of Ezra and is also named on the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah. His inclusion in these records highlights his involvement in the religious and communal reforms during the return from exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' reflecting a theologically significant name that acknowledges God's sovereignty and providence. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 8:19, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hashabiah was a descendant of Merari, one of the three main divisions of the Levites. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's significance lies in his role as a Levite entrusted with important responsibilities during the restoration period. Being sent to Ezra indicates his involvement in supporting the priestly and teaching functions essential for reestablishing proper worship. His name on the covenant document in Nehemiah underscores his commitment to the community's spiritual renewal and covenant faithfulness.
